title: How few bits can a MAC lane use to classify real handwritten digits before accuracy falls off a cliff?
lede: weight and activation bit-width sweep of a 64-16-10 quantised MLP on the scikit-learn digits data (5 splits), with the MAC lane's gate count from Yosys and its RTL checked against NumPy: 4-bit weights and activations lose about 2 points of accuracy, 5 and 5 about 0.5, below 3 bits it collapses.
summary: A 64-16-10 ReLU MLP trained on the real scikit-learn digits images (1797 8×8 scans, 70/30 splits, 5 seeds; float test accuracy 96.8%), quantised after training to W-bit signed weights and A-bit unsigned activations (W, A = 2–8, 49 configurations). One multiply-accumulate lane is written in Verilog, simulated in Icarus Verilog and matched to NumPy on 64 real layer-1 dot products per configuration (all 49 agree), and scored with Yosys and ABC in generic gates. Accuracy holds to 96.3% at W5A5 (268 cells, −0.5 points), 94.8% at W4A4 (189 cells, −2.0 points) and collapses at 3 bits or fewer (7978–82% at W3, 31–34% at W2ndash;82% at W3 with 3-bit or wider activations, 3178–82% at W3, 31–34% at W2ndash;34% at W2) or at 2-bit activations; widening beyond 6 bits buys nothing. Lane cells are not monotonic in width (ABC noise). Limitations: one small network and dataset, symmetric max-scaled quantisation with no quantisation-aware training (so the 2–3 bit collapse is a property of that scheme), generic-gate counts not square microns, one lane rather than a full accelerator, no clock, power or layout.
